posts.text:
Today I’m excited to introduce OpenDocRouter - a unified API for document parsing with the latest frontier and open-weight models.

There are a lot of VLMs and OCR models that can be used for document parsing: we have over 130+ models on ParseBench, and a HuggingFace search for “ocr” turns up thousands of results.

It’s extremely time consuming to choose between OCR vendors. You need to figure out the right prompts, handle rate limits, manage deployments, integrations with all models you’re using, and benchmark new models as they come out.

OpenDocRouter provides a comprehensive, transparent set of models along the price-performance frontier. It manages a unified API to transcribe documents to markdown. It serves all frontier and open-weight models “at-cost”, with a small transaction cut. It handles rate limits with all models to ensure you can put massive volume through. It even offers bounding boxes and layout as a service, so that you can add grounding to any model that you’re using.

When new OCR candidate models ship, we will benchmark them on ParseBench and immediately add them to OpenDocRouter. 

We’re adding a lot more models very quickly, and also adding some extremely exciting feature improvements (e.g. automated routing) as we speak.

We welcome your feedback!

Check it out: https://t.co/v8PieWWUNV

Blog: https://t.co/ilVqqJRacP

LLMs have crossed an important threshold: surpassing top human experts on some research problems. Capabilities have been steadily improving for years, but in scientific discovery there is a big difference between a model just below top human performance and one just above it. That helps explain why the surge in math results feels so sudden.

LLM capabilities remain jagged, and there are many ways they are still worse than humans. But as models continue to improve, I expect breakthroughs in other domains to follow, leading to a new era of scientific discovery.

posts.text:
AI 时代，怎么继续真正学习？

一句话，别让 AI替你思考，让它逼你思考。

作者在学习 Bitcask 和 LSM-tree 这类存储系统时，刻意不给 AI 直接写答案，而是让它当「苏格拉底式导师」，不断提问，把关键问题留给自己想。

测试、脚手架、可视化这些重复工作可以交给 AI，真正需要建立理解的部分自己啃。再让 AI 把大项目拆成一个个能验证的小阶段。

这个思路我非常喜欢。

以前学习难在找不到答案，现在更难的可能是答案来得太快。

AI 可以帮我们绕开很多没意义的弯路，但那些真正能长能力的地方，可能还是得给自己留一点「卡住」的时间。

reviewedPosts.text:
Today I’m excited to introduce OpenDocRouter - a unified API for document parsing with the latest frontier and open-weight models.

There are a lot of VLMs and OCR models that can be used for document parsing: we have over 130+ models on ParseBench, and a HuggingFace search for “ocr” turns up thousands of results.

It’s extremely time consuming to choose between OCR vendors. You need to figure out the right prompts, handle rate limits, manage deployments, integrations with all models you’re using, and benchmark new models as they come out.

OpenDocRouter provides a comprehensive, transparent set of models along the price-performance frontier. It manages a unified API to transcribe documents to markdown. It serves all frontier and open-weight models “at-cost”, with a small transaction cut. It handles rate limits with all models to ensure you can put massive volume through. It even offers bounding boxes and layout as a service, so that you can add grounding to any model that you’re using.

When new OCR candidate models ship, we will benchmark them on ParseBench and immediately add them to OpenDocRouter. 

We’re adding a lot more models very quickly, and also adding some extremely exciting feature improvements (e.g. automated routing) as we speak.

We welcome your feedback!

LLMs have crossed an important threshold: surpassing top human experts on some research problems. Capabilities have been steadily improving for years, but in scientific discovery there is a big difference between a model just below top human performance and one just above it. That helps explain why the surge in math results feels so sudden.

LLM capabilities remain jagged, and there are many ways they are still worse than humans. But as models continue to improve, I expect breakthroughs in other domains to follow, leading to a new era of scientific discovery.
